Key competencies include evaluating trigonometric ratios using SOH-CAH-TOA, exploiting the complementary cofunction identity \(\sin(x) = \cos(90^\circ - x)\), applying radian-degree conversions (\(180^\circ = \pi\text{ rad}\)), simplifying expressions using the Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\), and performing complex number arithmetic (\(i^2 = -1\)).

label.en: Definition 7.1 — Trigonometric Ratios, Radians, and the Complex Number System
label.ar: تعريف 7.1 — Trigonometric Ratios, Radians, and the Complex Number System

body.en:
Core definitions of trigonometric ratios and complex numbers:
  • Right-Triangle Trigonometric Ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA):
    For acute angle \(\theta\) in a right triangle:
    \[ \sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} \]
  • Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios:
    \[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Opp}}, \qquad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Adj}}, \qquad \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{\text{Adj}}{\text{Opp}} \]
  • Radian Measure: One radian is the measure of a central angle that intercepts an arc equal in length to the circle's radius. The conversion equivalence is:
    \[ \pi\text{ radians} = 180^\circ \implies 1\text{ rad} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}, \quad 1^\circ = \frac{\pi}{180^\circ}\text{ rad} \]
  • Complex Number System (\(\mathbb{C}\)):
    A complex number has standard form \(z = a + bi\), where \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) such that \(i^2 = -1\).
    1. Powers of \(i\) (Cyclic modulo 4): \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\).
    2. Complex Conjugate: \(\bar{z} = a - bi\), with real product \(z \bar{z} = a^2 + b^2\).
    3. Modulus: \(|z| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\).
body.ar:
Core definitions of trigonometric ratios and complex numbers:
  • Right-المثلث Trigonometric Ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA):
    For acute الزاوية \(\theta\) in a right المثلث:
    \[ \sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}, \qquad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} \]
  • Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios:
    \[ \csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Opp}}, \qquad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\text{Hyp}}{\text{Adj}}, \qquad \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta} = \frac{\text{Adj}}{\text{Opp}} \]
  • Radian Measure: One radian is the measure of a central الزاوية that intercepts an arc equal in length to the الدائرة's نصف القطر. The conversion equivalence is:
    \[ \pi\text{ radians} = 180^\circ \implies 1\text{ rad} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}, \quad 1^\circ = \frac{\pi}{180^\circ}\text{ rad} \]
  • Complex Number System (\(\mathbb{C}\)):
    A complex number has standard form \(z = a + bi\), حيث \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) such that \(i^2 = -1\).
    1. Powers of \(i\) (Cyclic modulo 4): \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\).
    2. Complex Conjugate: \(\bar{z} = a - bi\), with real product \(z \bar{z} = a^2 + b^2\).
    3. Modulus: \(|z| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\).

body.en: Unit Circle Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & Triangle Laws: Every angle \(\theta\) on the unit circle defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) where \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).
body.ar: Unit الدائرة Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & المثلث Laws: Every الزاوية \(\theta\) on the unit الدائرة defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) حيث \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

label.en: Theorem 7.1 — Cofunction Complementarity, Pythagorean Identities, and Complex Division
label.ar: مبرهنة 7.1 — Cofunction Complementarity, Pythagorean المتطابقات, and Complex Division

body.en:
Fundamental identities and algebraic procedures:
  • Complementary Angle Theorem (Cofunction Identity):
    In any right triangle with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(A + B = 90^\circ\) (or \(\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ rad}\)):
    \[ \sin A = \cos(90^\circ - A) = \cos B \]
    \[ \cos A = \sin(90^\circ - A) = \sin B \]
    \[ \tan A = \cot(90^\circ - A) = \frac{1}{\tan B} \]
  • Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities:
    1. \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\)
    2. \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\)
    3. \(1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta\)
  • Special Right Triangle Values (Unit Circle):
    1. \(30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}\): \(\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\tan 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\).
    2. \(45^\circ = \frac{\pi}{4}\): \(\sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), \(\cos 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\).
    3. \(60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}\): \(\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), \(\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\).
  • Division of Complex Numbers: Multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator to eliminate \(i\) from the denominator:
    \[ \frac{a + bi}{c + di} = \frac{(a + bi)(c - di)}{(c + di)(c - di)} = \frac{(ac + bd) + (bc - ad)i}{c^2 + d^2} \]

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Trigonometry & Additional Topics
label.ar: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — حساب المثلثات & Additional Topics

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Mode: If evaluating trigonometric ratios on a calculator, always verify your active mode! Evaluating \(\sin(30)\) in radian mode yields \(-0.988\) instead of \(0.5\).
  • Complementary Angle Theorem: In any right triangle, the acute angles sum to \(90^\circ\), which implies \(\sin(x) = \cos(90^\circ - x)\) and \(\cos(x) = \sin(90^\circ - x)\). If \(\sin(A) = \cos(B)\), then \(A + B = 90^\circ\).
  • Pythagorean Identity Variations: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) rearranges to \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)\). Recognizing this difference of squares simplifies many algebraic trig questions instantly.
  • Powers of \(i\) Cyclicity: Powers of the imaginary unit cycle every 4 powers: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). To evaluate \(i^n\), divide \(n\) by 4 and use the remainder.
  • Complex Multiplication Errors: Remember that \(i^2 = -1\), so \((a + bi)^2 = a^2 + 2abi + b^2 i^2 = (a^2 - b^2) + 2abi\). Do NOT write \(a^2 + b^2\) for the square of a binomial!
body.ar:

  • Pythagorean المتطابقة Variations: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) rearranges to \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)\). Recognizing this difference of squares simplifies many algebraic trig questions instantly.
  • Powers of \(i\) Cyclicity: Powers of the imaginary unit cycle every 4 powers: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). To احسب قيمة \(i^n\), divide \(n\) by 4 and use the remainder.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Trigonometry & Additional Topics)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (حساب المثلثات & Additional Topics)

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).
body.ar:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-الصيغة & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-الزاوية المتطابقة gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching المعاملات with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

label.en: Worked Example 7.A — Cofunction Equalities & Angle Algebra
label.ar: مثال محلول 7.A — Cofunction Equalities & الزاوية الجبر

body.en:
In a right triangle with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\), it is given that \(\sin(4x - 10^\circ) = \cos(3x + 16^\circ)\).
(a) Find the value of \(x\).
(b) Determine the exact value of \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Use the Cofunction Complementarity Theorem:
    Since \(\sin(u) = \cos(v)\) for acute angles, the two angles are complementary: \[ u + v = 90^\circ \]
    Substitute the expressions:
    \[ (4x - 10^\circ) + (3x + 16^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 7x + 6^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 7x = 84^\circ \implies \mathbf{x = 12^\circ} \]
  2. (b) Evaluate \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\):
    Substitute \(x = 12^\circ\):
    \[ \sin(12^\circ + 18^\circ) = \sin(30^\circ) = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2} = 0.5} \]
body.ar:
In a right المثلث with acute angles \(A\) and \(B\), it is بما أن \(\sin(4x - 10^\circ) = \cos(3x + 16^\circ)\).
(a) أوجد قيمة \(x\).
(b) حدّد exact value of \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Use the Cofunction Complementarity مبرهنة:
    Since \(\sin(u) = \cos(v)\) for acute angles, the two angles are complementary: \[ u + v = 90^\circ \]

    \[ (4x - 10^\circ) + (3x + 16^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 7x + 6^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 7x = 84^\circ \implies \mathbf{x = 12^\circ} \]
  2. (b) احسب قيمة \(\sin(x + 18^\circ)\):
    Substitute \(x = 12^\circ\):
    \[ \sin(12^\circ + 18^\circ) = \sin(30^\circ) = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2} = 0.5} \]

body.en:
Simplify the expression \(\dfrac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta}\) and express it in terms of a single fundamental trigonometric function.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Recall the Pythagorean identity: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta\).
  2. Substitute \(\sin^2\theta\) into the numerator:
    \[ \frac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta} \]
  3. Cancel one factor of \(\sin\theta\) from numerator and denominator:
    \[ \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\tan\theta} \]
The simplified expression is \(\mathbf{\tan\theta}\).
body.ar:
بسّط العبارة \(\dfrac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta \cos\theta}\) and express it in terms of a single fundamental trigonometric الدالة.

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Recall the Pythagorean المتطابقة: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta\).
  2. Substitute \(\sin^2\theta\) into the numerator:

  3. Cancel one factor of \(\sin\theta\) from numerator and denominator:
    \[ \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\tan\theta} \]
The simplified العبارة الجبرية is \(\mathbf{\tan\theta}\).

label.en: Worked Example 7.C — Complex Number Operations & Rationalization
label.ar: مثال محلول 7.C — Complex Number Operations & Rationalization

body.en:
(a) Express the quotient \(\dfrac{7 + 4i}{2 - 3i}\) in standard complex form \(a + bi\).
(b) Evaluate the sum of powers \(i^{2024} + i^{2025} + i^{2026} + i^{2027}\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Multiply by the conjugate \(2 + 3i\):
    \[ \frac{7 + 4i}{2 - 3i} = \frac{(7 + 4i)(2 + 3i)}{(2 - 3i)(2 + 3i)} \]
    Expand denominator: \(2^2 - (3i)^2 = 4 - 9(-1) = 4 + 9 = 13\).
    Expand numerator using FOIL:
    \[ (7)(2) + 21i + 8i + 12i^2 = 14 + 29i + 12(-1) = (14 - 12) + 29i = 2 + 29i \]
    Divide both parts by 13:
    \[ \mathbf{\frac{2}{13} + \frac{29}{13}i} \]
  2. (b) Evaluate sum of powers of \(i\):
    Any four consecutive integer powers of \(i\) sum to 0:
    Since \(2024 = 4 \times 506\) (remainder 0): \(i^{2024} = 1\).
    \(i^{2025} = i\), \(i^{2026} = -1\), \(i^{2027} = -i\).
    \[ 1 + i - 1 - i = \mathbf{0} \]

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Trigonometry & Additional Topics (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — حساب المثلثات & Additional Topics (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): In the right-angled triangle ABC shown below, \( \angle ABC = 90^{\circ} \), \( AB = 3 \), and \( BC = 4 \). What is the length of the hypotenuse AC?

Step-by-Step Solution: This question involves a direct application of the Pythagorean theorem in a right-angled triangle. The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. In triangle ABC, with \( \angle ABC = 90^{\circ} \), AB and BC are the two shorter sides (legs), and AC is the hypotenuse. According to the Pythagorean theorem: \[ AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \] Given \( AB = 3 \) and \( BC = 4 \): \[ AC^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 \] \[ AC^2 = 9 + 16 \] \[ AC^2 = 25 \] To find the length of AC, we take the square root of both sides: \[ AC = \sqrt{25} \] \[ AC = 5 \] Therefore, the length of the hypotenuse AC is 5.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): In the right-angled المثلث ABC shown below, \( \angle ABC = 90^{\circ} \), \( AB = 3 \), and \( BC = 4 \). What is the length of the hypotenuse AC?

Step-by-Step الحل: This question involves a direct application of the Pythagorean المبرهنة in a right-angled المثلث. The Pythagorean المبرهنة states that in a right-angled المثلث, the square of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right الزاوية) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. In المثلث ABC, with \( \angle ABC = 90^{\circ} \), AB and BC are the two shorter sides (legs), and AC is the hypotenuse. According to the Pythagorean المبرهنة: \[ AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \] المعطيات \( AB = 3 \) and \( BC = 4 \): \[ AC^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 \] \[ AC^2 = 9 + 16 \] \[ AC^2 = 25 \] To أوجد length of AC, we take the square root of both sides: \[ AC = \sqrt{25} \] \[ AC = 5 \] وبالتالي, the length of the hypotenuse AC is 5.

question.en: In a right triangle, acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}\). Find the exact values of \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\), and \(\sec\theta\).
question.ar: In a right triangle, acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}\). أوجد exact values of \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\), and \(\sec\theta\).

solution.en:
Step 1: In a right triangle with opposite side \(5\) and hypotenuse \(13\), the adjacent side is: \[ \text{adj} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12. \]

Step 2: Compute trigonometric ratios:

  • \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{12}{13}}\).
  • \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{5}{12}}\).
  • \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\dfrac{13}{12}}\).
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية:

Step 1: In a right triangle with opposite side \(5\) and hypotenuse \(13\), the adjacent side is: \[ \text{adj} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12. \]

Step 2: Compute trigonometric ratios:

  • \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{12}{13}}\).
  • \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}} = \mathbf{\dfrac{5}{12}}\).
  • \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} = \mathbf{\dfrac{13}{12}}\).

question.en: If \(\cos(2x + 10^\circ) = \sin(3x - 15^\circ)\), find the value of \(x\) and evaluate \(\tan(x + 16^\circ)\).
question.ar: إذا كان \(\cos(2x + 10^\circ) = \sin(3x - 15^\circ)\), أوجد قيمة \(x\) and احسب قيمة \(\tan(x + 16^\circ)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply cofunction identity \(\cos A = \sin B \iff A + B = 90^\circ\): \[ (2x + 10^\circ) + (3x - 15^\circ) = 90^\circ \implies 5x - 5^\circ = 90^\circ \implies 5x = 95^\circ \implies \mathbf{x = 19^\circ}. \]

Step 2: Evaluate tangent: \[ \tan(19^\circ + 16^\circ) = \tan(35^\circ) \approx \mathbf{0.7002}. \]
solution.ar:

Step 2: احسب قيمة tangent: \[ \tan(19^\circ + 16^\circ) = \tan(35^\circ) \approx \mathbf{0.7002}. \]

question.en: Convert \(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) radians to degrees, and find the exact coordinates of its terminal point on the unit circle.
question.ar: Convert \(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) radians to degrees, and أوجد exact coordinates of its terminal point on the unit circle.

solution.en:
Step 1: Convert to degrees: \[ \theta = \frac{7\pi}{6} \times \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} = 7 \times 30^\circ = \mathbf{210^\circ}. \]

Step 2: Terminal coordinates in Quadrant III: The reference angle is \(210^\circ - 180^\circ = 30^\circ\). In Quadrant III, both coordinates are negative: \[ x = \cos(210^\circ) = -\cos(30^\circ) = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \qquad y = \sin(210^\circ) = -\sin(30^\circ) = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

The terminal point is \(\mathbf{\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)}\).
solution.ar:

question.en: Evaluate the complex expression \(\dfrac{(3 - 2i)^2}{1 + i}\) and write the result in standard form \(a + bi\).
question.ar: احسب قيمة the complex expression \(\dfrac{(3 - 2i)^2}{1 + i}\) and write the result in standard form \(a + bi\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Expand the numerator: \[ (3 - 2i)^2 = 3^2 - 2(3)(2i) + (2i)^2 = 9 - 12i + 4(-1) = 5 - 12i. \]

Step 2: Multiply by conjugate \(1 - i\): \[ \frac{5 - 12i}{1 + i} = \frac{(5 - 12i)(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)} = \frac{5 - 5i - 12i + 12i^2}{1 - i^2} = \frac{5 - 17i - 12}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-7 - 17i}{2}. \]

In standard form: \(\mathbf{-\frac{7}{2} - \frac{17}{2}i}\).
solution.ar:
Step 1: فكّ المقدار the numerator: \[ (3 - 2i)^2 = 3^2 - 2(3)(2i) + (2i)^2 = 9 - 12i + 4(-1) = 5 - 12i. \]

Step 2: Multiply by conjugate \(1 - i\): \[ \frac{5 - 12i}{1 + i} = \frac{(5 - 12i)(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)} = \frac{5 - 5i - 12i + 12i^2}{1 - i^2} = \frac{5 - 17i - 12}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-7 - 17i}{2}. \]

In standard form: \(\mathbf{-\frac{7}{2} - \frac{17}{2}i}\).

question.en: If \( i = \sqrt{-1} \), what is the value of \( i^{197} \)?
question.ar: إذا كان \( i = \sqrt{-1} \), ما قيمة \( i^{197} \)?

hints.en: The powers of the imaginary unit \( i \) repeat in a cycle of length 4: \( i^1 = i \), \( i^2 = -1 \), \( i^3 = -i \), \( i^4 = 1 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( i \) ، \( i^1 = i \) ، \( i^2 = -1 \) ، \( i^3 = -i \) ، \( i^4 = 1 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(197 = 4 \times 49 + 1\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
The powers of the imaginary unit \( i \) repeat in a cycle of length 4:
\( i^1 = i \), \( i^2 = -1 \), \( i^3 = -i \), \( i^4 = 1 \).
Divide the exponent 197 by 4:
\[ 197 = 4 \times 49 + 1 \]
Thus, \( i^{197} = (i^4)^{49} \times i^{1} = (1)^{49} \times i^{1} = i \).
solution.ar:
The powers of the imaginary unit \( i \) repeat in a cycle of length 4:
\( i^1 = i \), \( i^2 = -1 \), \( i^3 = -i \), \( i^4 = 1 \).
Divide the exponent 197 by 4:
\[ 197 = 4 \times 49 + 1 \]
وعليه، \( i^{197} = (i^4)^{49} \times i^{1} = (1)^{49} \times i^{1} = i \).

label.ar: ● الدليل الشامل للنسب المثلثية الست — دائرة الوحدة والمقلوبات والمجالات والدورات وخطوط التقارب

body.en:
For any angle \( heta\) in standard position whose terminal ray intersects the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) at \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (or a right triangle with opposite \(o\), adjacent \(a\), and hypotenuse \(h\)), the six trigonometric functions are:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
FunctionDomainRangePeriodSymmetryVertical Asymptotes
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)OddNone
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)EvenNone
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Even\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)

Pythagorean Identities: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\), \(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\), and \(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).
body.ar:
لأي زاوية \( heta\) في الوضع القياسي يقطع ضلع انتهائها دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) عند النقطة \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (أو في مثلث قائم الزاوية بمقابل \(o\) ومجاور \(a\) ووتر \(h\))، تُعرَّف الدوال المثلثية الست كما يلي:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
الدالةالمجالالمدىالدورة الأساسيةالتماثلخطوط التقارب الرأسية

\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)زوجيةلا يوجد
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)زوجية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)

متطابقات فيثاغورس المثلثية: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\)، و\(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\)، و\(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).

label.ar: ● الدوال المثلثية العكسية الست جميعاً — المجالات المقيدة والمدى الأساسي

body.en:
Because the six trigonometric functions are periodic, they are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\). Restricting each forward function to its canonical principal branch makes it strictly monotonic so that a unique inverse exists (whose graph is the reflection of the restricted branch across \(y = x\)):

Inverse FunctionEquivalent StatementDomain of \(f^{-1}(x)\)Principal Range (Radians)Unit Circle Quadrants
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)Quadrants I & II

Reciprocal & Cofunction Identities: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) and \(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) for \(|x| \ge 1\); \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
body.ar:
نظراً لأن الدوال المثلثية الست دورية، فإنها ليست متباينة (واحداً لواحد) على \(\mathbb{R}\). بتقييد مجال كل دالة إلى فرعها الأساسي تصبح رتيبة تماماً وقابلة للعكس، ويكون تمثيل الدالة العكسية انعكاساً للفرع المقيّد حول المستقيم \(y = x\):

الدالة العكسيةالصيغة المكافئةمجال \(f^{-1}(x)\)المدى الأساسي (بالراديان)أرباع دائرة الوحدة
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)الربعان الأول والثاني

متطابقات المقلوبات والدوال المتممة: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) و\(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) لكل \(|x| \ge 1\)؛ وكذلك \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) و\(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
